messages.subject: DSM relative variable importance
parts:
Hi all, 
I was trying to get the relative variable importance of the variables in my density surface model but it doesn't seem to work for some reasons. I'm using a smoothing function for X and Y and I'm testing 4 other variables without smoothing (these are the variables for which). 
Here is my code: 

Model<-dsm(density.est ~  
             s(X, Y, k=8)+
             Rec_350+
             Grass_630+
             DistArable+
             Calc_130,  
           ddf.obj=Hr_vis100, 
           segment.data=Section, 
           observation.data=Roe_obs,
           method="REML", na.action="na.fail")

Dredged<- dredge(Model)

Model_averaging<-model.avg(Dredged)

summary(Model_averaging)$importance

This is the output I get:

                              Calc_130   DistArable   Grass_630   Rec_350   s(X, Y, k = 8)
Importance:               NA                NA               NA             NA              NA            
N containing models: 16                16                16              16               16     

Basically I don't have the variable importance. 

Thank you in advance!!
Valentina

Seems your challenge might be with the dredge() function, rather than the dsm() function.  I don't know that function, nor the package it comes from.


It is not obvious to me that dsm(), particularly when using REML, has the model structure that this model.avg() function can process.

Yes, you are right the issue should be in the dredge function. 
I've looked into the MuMIn package and it says that dredge can process GAMs, so it should be able to process the DSM as it is a GAM object. I couldn't find much information about model averaging in GAMs anyway. I wonder if anybody has tried it yet. 
Valentina

messages.subject: {Disarmed} Re[2]: [distance-sampling] DSM relative variable importance
parts:
Valentina

As I said, I don't know what dredge() is looking for, but the object produced by dsm is a 2-part object; part gam and part ddf object.  As described in documentation:

Value

a MailScanner has detected a possible fraud attempt from "127.0.0.1:38836" claiming to be glm/MailScanner has detected a possible fraud attempt from "127.0.0.1:38836" claiming to be gam/MailScanner has detected a possible fraud attempt from "127.0.0.1:38836" claiming to be gamm object, with an additional element, ddf which holds the detection function object.


Perhaps you need to tear off the gam part of the dsm object to pass to your magic function.


------
